_comment: External (non-package-manager) dependencies this codebase tracks pinned versions/commits of. check_dependency_releases.py reads this file and reports when upstream has moved past the pinned point. 'release' mode compares against GitHub's latest-release tag; 'branch' mode compares against a tracked branch's current HEAD commit (used when we deliberately build from a branch other than the default, e.g. a bug fix that only landed on 'develop'). IMPORTANT: 'pinned' means the last version this codebase's own real test suite was actually run against and confirmed working -- not whatever happens to be currently installed/deployed, and never a value copied from a fresh API query without also re-running the tests against it. Bump 'pinned' only after a real verification pass.

pat.pinned_via: real v1.0.0 release tarball, PATH-overridden and run against the full hams_local_relay suite this session (209/209 passing)
pat.notes: Winlink client subprocess. v1.0.0 added an interactive account-activation confirmation prompt that hung every real pat-connect test until spawn_pat_connect() was fixed to pipe "c\n" to stdin -- found only by re-running the real tests, not by reading the changelog (which didn't mention it). The system-installed Debian package is still v0.16.0; the stdin fix is backward-compatible with it (verified separately, 35/35 passing) so this pin intentionally tracks the newer, fully-verified version rather than what happens to be deployed.

ardopcf.notes: Deliberately tracking 'develop', not 'master' or the latest numbered release -- master still has a known, already-fixed-upstream build bug (GCC14 rejects lib/rawhid/rawhid.c's pointer/int mismatch; see pflarue/ardop issues #124 and #162) that was never merged from develop to master. See check-upstream-issues-before-filing lesson before assuming any future ardopcf build error is novel.

mercury.notes: GPL-3.0, run as an isolated subprocess (see DATAC_TRANSPORT_INTEGRATION.md's GPL-isolation section) -- never linked into hams_local_relay itself, so a version bump here is a pure behavior/compatibility question, not a licensing one.

hamlib.pinned_via: system package (libhamlib-dev) used to build mercury and referenced by hamlib.rs
hamlib.notes: Currently tracked via distro package, not built from source -- this entry records the upstream release we last verified compatibility against, not a build pin.
